claims.text: SLM/PBF-LB/M can be used to fabricate refractory high-entropy alloy parts based on Nb, Ta, W, Mo, and V.
A high scan speed combined with a small hatch distance produces a high temperature gradient and low growth rate.
Parameter Set B from PMC8201384 represents the proposed high-scan-speed, small-hatch-distance strategy.
High temperature gradient and low growth rate favor an almost cellular rather than coarse dendritic solidification structure.
Rapid solidification during SLM produces fine grains and reduced dendrite-arm spacing compared with casting.
The high cooling rate in SLM suppresses the formation of coarse Laves phases and other brittle intermetallics.
Using a controlled, low vanadium concentration will produce a VEC below 4.4.
A VEC below 4.4 stabilizes a single-phase BCC refractory alloy and improves mechanical performance.
Keeping O, N, and C concentrations low prevents embrittlement through oxide or nitride formation.
A high-temperature post-processing anneal can dissolve or reduce brittle Laves phases.
The proposed anneal can generate a coherent nanoscale precipitate distribution.
The proposed high-temperature anneal will retain the SLM cellular structure without excessive coarsening.
Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission, relieve stress concentrations, and reduce premature crack initiation while strengthening the alloy.
The cellular coherent-precipitate state will replace brittle Laves phases or coarse dendritic structures in the proposed alloy.
Laves phases and related refractory intermetallic compounds can be brittle and reduce mechanical performance.
The resulting alloy will retain ductility and structural integrity at high temperature.
A fine cellular grain structure will enhance strength through grain-boundary strengthening.
Conventionally cast refractory HEAs have substantially coarser grains and dendrite-arm spacing than rapidly solidified SLM material.
Arc-melted refractory HEAs generally contain grain-boundary Laves phases that cause poor ductility and limited high-temperature performance.
FCC-to-monoclinic phase instability has been observed in the relevant refractory alloy family.

contradictions.description: The proposed route specifies high scan speed and identifies it with Parameter Set B, but the cited Parameter Set B used low scan speed and produced the cellular structure; the higher-growth-rate parameter set produced the coarser dendritic structure.
The alloy is described as a Group IV–V transition-metal family while the listed constituents include Mo and W, which are not Group IV–V elements.
